answer: Edge-disjoint path quota. Each agent’s action budget scales with edge-disjoint routes to fixed anchors, recomputed from topology. Clones sharing one upstream link add no new signal, so spawning identities gives no extra budget. To raise quota, an attacker must rent and maintain distinct paths per cluster, paying separate route costs. A single pearl of connectivity cannot substitute for many independent routes. Clones behind one jetty collapse to one route. Per-identity cost is independent-path rent plus upkeep, not registration.
